report.summary: Parsing abstraction module with three backends: Python ast, tree-sitter, and fallback window clone. Contains CodeUnit dataclass, extract_units, python_units_and_imports, tree-sitter helpers, and import resolution. All docstring claims checked against visible code.

handoff.purpose: Define parsing abstraction for extracting code units and imports per language.

symbols.name: CodeUnit
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with fields: language, module, name, line, end_line, loc, source.

symbols.name: tree_sitter_available
symbols.note: LRU-cached function returning True if tree_sitter_language_pack can be imported.

symbols.name: _parser_for
symbols.note: Cached function returning parser for a grammar, or None on failure.

symbols.name: extract_units
symbols.note: Returns list of CodeUnit for given module, text, and LanguageSpec.

symbols.name: _python_units
symbols.note: Parses Python text with ast, returns CodeUnits for functions and async functions.

symbols.name: _units_from_tree
symbols.note: Walks AST tree to collect FunctionDef and AsyncFunctionDef nodes.

symbols.name: python_units_and_imports
symbols.note: Returns tuple of CodeUnits and import records from single AST parse.

symbols.name: _tree_sitter_units
symbols.note: Uses tree-sitter parser to extract CodeUnits for languages other than Python.

symbols.name: _ANON
symbols.note: String constant '<anonymous>' used as fallback name.

symbols.name: _DECL_WRAPPERS
symbols.note: Tuple of declarator wrapper node types for C/C++.

symbols.name: _DECL_NAME_TYPES
symbols.note: Tuple of node types that can be function names in C/C++.

symbols.name: _decl_text
symbols.note: Extracts name text from a declarator node, handling operator_cast specially.

symbols.name: _declarator_name
symbols.note: Walks C/C++ declarator chain to find function name, depth-limited.

symbols.name: _ts_name
symbols.note: Extracts function name from a tree-sitter node, trying named field then children.

symbols.name: _import_records
symbols.note: Returns raw unresolved import records from AST tree.

symbols.name: python_import_records
symbols.note: Parses text and returns import records.

symbols.name: resolve_python_imports
symbols.note: Resolves raw import records to internal dotted modules.

claims.text: Three backends, chosen automatically: Python -> stdlib ast (always available, precise). others -> tree-sitter via tree_sitter_language_pack IF installed. neither -> no unit-level extraction; the caller falls back to the universal windowed clone pass (see clones.window_clones), which needs no parser.
claims.why: extract_units implements exactly this: for python uses _python_units, for others checks ts_grammar and tree_sitter_available, else returns [].

claims.text: The unit source returned here is what clones.fingerprint hashes, so this is the precision lever: with tree-sitter, C/Java/Rust/… get real function-level clone detection; without it, they still get window-level detection.
claims.why: Refers to clones.fingerprint and window-level detection not present in this chunk.

claims.text: This module ALSO carries the type/data-structure extractor (see the section at the bottom: PyTypeFacts and friends). It lives here and not in a sibling module for one non-negotiable reason: cache.file_key mixes a sha256 of *this file, by name* into every disk-cache key, so an edit to the extractor invalidates every cached row. An extractor in a sibling module would leave the key untouched and serve rows written by the PREVIOUS extractor to the new code -- wrong type blocks, no error, no log line.
claims.why: Refers to PyTypeFacts and cache.file_key not present in this chunk.

claims.text: What the extractor produces is raw and unresolved: classes, fields, signatures and import NAME bindings as written, with every annotation kept as a RAW STRING. Resolution is whole-repo work and happens in the parent process, one layer up.
claims.why: Refers to extractor output not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: C/C++ hide the function name where no other grammar puts it. There is no ``name`` field on ``function_definition``; the name sits at the bottom of a ``declarator`` chain:
claims.why: _ts_name checks for 'name' field first, then falls back to 'declarator' field, consistent with claim.

claims.text: the chain can be arbitrarily long, because pointer/reference/array returns each interpose a wrapper (``void *bar()`` adds pointer_declarator).
claims.why: _declarator_name walks up to 16 levels through _DECL_WRAPPERS types, acknowledging arbitrary length.

claims.text: Meanwhile the RETURN TYPE is a plain ``type_identifier`` sitting as a direct child of the same node -- which is why the generic direct-children scan below used to return "MyType" for "MyType foo(void)". That is worse than no name: every function returning MyType collides on one identifier, and unlike "<anonymous>" a fabricated name is NOT filtered out of the clone passes. Hence: once a ``declarator`` field exists, its chain is authoritative and we never fall through to the scan.
claims.why: _ts_name first checks 'declarator' field before falling through to children scan, and _decl_text handles operator_cast. The comment describes past behavior, now corrected.

claims.text: ``operator bool()`` is the one shape whose name node spans more than the name: the grammar's ``operator_cast`` covers the parameter list and cv qualifiers too, so slicing it whole yields "operator bool() const". Cut at the end of its ``type`` field instead -> "operator bool" (and, when it is wrapped in a qualified_identifier, "Foo::operator bool").
claims.why: _decl_text checks if node.type == 'operator_cast', then gets child 'type' and returns data from node.start_byte to that child's end_byte, trimming the extra.

claims.text: A function returning a function pointer -- "int (*get_handler(int))(void)" -- nests a SECOND function_declarator inside parentheses, and which of the two is "the function being defined" is genuinely ambiguous. Guessing here would fabricate a name, so under-report instead.
claims.why: _declarator_name checks for 'parenthesized_declarator' and returns _ANON, as stated.

claims.text: reference_declarator ("std::string& Cfg::name()") carries its inner declarator as an unnamed child rather than a labelled field.
claims.why: When nxt is None after field lookup, it falls back to next named child, which handles unnamed children.

claims.text: Deliberately independent of ``internal_tops``/``known`` — those are derived from the whole file set, so they are not available until every file has been collected. Keeping extraction (per-file, expensive, parallelizable) apart from resolution (whole-repo, cheap, serial) is what lets the parse run in a worker process while resolution stays in the parent.
claims.why: _import_records returns raw tuples without any resolution, as described. resolve_python_imports takes internal_tops and known as parameters.

claims.text: Handles both absolute (``from daedalus.core import x``) and RELATIVE (``from .router import x``, ``from ..core import y``) imports — the latter anchored to ``src_dotted`` (this file's own dotted module), which is essential inside packages that use relative imports heavily.
claims.why: The function body is cut off; only the first few lines are visible. The handling of relative imports with src_dotted is not fully implemented in the visible chunk.
